expectations.note: After clearing the Dot preference and restarting, the live screenshot shows the pulsing dot without any artist/title overlay.
The toggle was enabled, survived a restart, and the resumed long-metadata track rendered the overlay afterward.
After explicitly turning the option off and restarting, the live long-metadata hero showed no overlay.
At 100%, the long artist/title overlay visibly occupies the same region as the centered pulsing dot, though the text is otherwise rendered.
At 150%, the overlay is visibly intersected by the dot and the title's lower line is cut at the hero boundary.
A fresh 100% reproduction was captured, but the candidate supplied no screenshot deliverable and the reproduced long overlay fails the no-overlap criterion.
A fresh 150% reproduction was captured, but the candidate supplied no screenshot deliverable and the reproduced long overlay fails both overlap and clipping criteria.
Probe/tree reads at normal and maximum scales show non-empty hero-artist and hero-song text with non-zero sizes; max probe reports 45px/816x106 and 22.5px/816x54.
Short fixture metadata renders at both scales without clipping, but the centered dot still visibly intersects the artist text in both captures.
After repeated toggling, restarts, scale changes, and long/short track switches, the app remained live with zero overflow reports.
